Take American Cheese, the real stuff, not the cheese food stuff, and break into 4 squares.

Place on some parchment paper, not wax paper, and nuke for 40-45 seconds, or until browned nicely throughout. This will take some experimenting, as the time varies quite a bit with the ambient humidity.

Remove immediately from the microwave and take them off of the parchment paper and place upside down. This will allow them to dry out.

Enjoy alone or spread with a small amount of peanut butter to make peanut butter "crackers".

This requires executing three steps, which I have explained below.

Outgoing firewall rules if needed

pfSense has this by default, unless you changed it. I am mentioning it just-in-case, so I won't spend much time on this.

Make sure that your firewall has the following rule enabled for LAN (Firewall -> Rules -> LAN):

IPv4 * LAN net * * * * none

This allows all packets to exit your LAN to the internet. If you are customizing your firewall rules, then TL2 uses outgoing target ports TCP 4549 and UDP 4175, 4179, 4171.

Set port forwarding

TL2 accepts connections on a custom UDP port you have to configure (you must configure it, or it will use a random port). In your C:\Users[YOUR USERNAME HERE]\Documents\my games\Runic Games\Torchlight 2\local_settings.txt find the line UDPORT :0 and set it to something like "UDPORT :11000". Remember: you cannot edit the file while the game is running (game will overwrite it on exit). Also edit with notepad to make sure you keep the file encoding - if you break the encoding, you can just delete the file. The game will recreate it on start.

If you set UDPORT to 11000, then this is the port number you will forward.

If you have more than one LAN user, you will have to forward a different port for each TL2 computer. You will also have to do step 3 for each TL2 computer.

In pfSense, go to Firewall -> NAT -> Port Forward. Set a port forward rule, which should look like this after it is created:

WAN UDP * * WAN address 11000 192.168.xxx.xxx 11000

This means:

Interface: WAN

Protocol: UDP

Source: any

Destination: WAN address

Redirect target IP: local IP address of your TL2 computer

Redirect target port: 11000

Destination port range: from 11000 to 11000

After the port is created, you might also want to check your filter rule and make sure you have the rule using the right QoS queue, if you are using QoS. Click on "View the filter rule" and scroll to Ackqueue/Queue, set the Queue to the one you want.

Create a rule in outbound NAT

This is the part most people miss. pfSense will randomize all outgoing ports. This presumably slightly increases security, but also breaks a bunch of applications, including TL2.

Go to Firewall -> NAT -> Outbound. Make sure you have "Manual Outbound NAT rule generation"

Then add a new rule, which should look like that in the list after it is created: 

WAN 192.168.xxx.xxx/32 * * * WAN address * YES

This will disable all port randomization on packets coming from your local LAN IP 192.168.xxx.xxx; if you really want to you could make the rule not randomize just the TL2 ports, but I have not tested that. Here are some more details about that rule:

Interface: WAN

Protocol: any

Source: Network, IP address of TL2 machine, /32

Source port: leave blank

Destination: any

Translation: Interface address, make sure to leave port blank and check static port. Making the port static stops pfSense from randomizing the ports.
